recipes.name: Mom’s Fabulous Chicken Pot Pie with Biscuit Crust
ingredients_raw: 3 cups cooked chicken, cut into bite-size pieces
salt and ground black pepper to taste
1 (16.3 ounce) can refrigerated flaky-style biscuits (such as Pillsbury Grands®)

steps.text: Gather the ingredients. Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).

Melt butter in a skillet over medium-low heat. Add onion, celery, and carrots and cook, stirring occasionally, until tender, about 15 minutes. Stir in peas, flour, parsley, and thyme and cook, stirring constantly, until the flour coats the vegetables and begins to fry, about 5 minutes.
Whisk in chicken broth and half-and-half, and cook until the sauce is thick and bubbling. Stir in cooked chicken, and season with salt and pepper.
Transfer chicken, vegetables, and sauce into a 7x11-inch baking dish. Arrange biscuits on top of the filling. Beat egg yolk with water in a small bowl. Brush mixture over the biscuits.
Bake in the preheated oven until the biscuits are golden brown and the pie filling is bubbly, 20 to 25 minutes. Remove from the oven and let rest for 10 minutes before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Mom’s Fabulous Chicken Pot Pie with Biscuit Crust
raw_recipe.description: This delicious chicken pot pie with biscuits is a comforting dinner that’s quick to make with cooked chicken and simple ingredients from your kitchen.

video.description: When the weather’s chilly, nothing is so comforting as a pot pie! Dispense with all the busy work and use refrigerator biscuits instead of pie crust and you’ll be on your way to a hearty meal in no time. Cook onion, celery and carrots in butter, then add peas, parsley, thyme and flour. Add half-and-half until a sauce forms. Salt and pepper, add bite size pieces of chicken and transfer to a baking dish. Top with biscuits, finish with an egg wash and bake until the biscuit topping is golden brown, the filling is bubbly and your home is filled with the tempting fragrance of fresh-baked pot pie!

review.reviewBody: My husband is currently eating his fourth bowl of this stuff, no lie. I actually made the whole deal in my cast iron skillet--sauteed, simmered, added biscuits and stuck it in the oven. Turned out perfectly and made a neat presentation, as well.
Winner, Winner, Chicken dinner. Added 3 yukon gold potatoes diced and 1/2 of a bell pepper with the rest of the veggies. Did it all in a dutch oven, from stove top then into oven. Awesome recipe.

Wow! This is so darn good! I followed the suggestions of a few other folks and did the whole thing in a big cast iron skillet. I baked the biscuits separately for 7 minutes, then transferred them to the skillet and tossed the whole thing in the oven at 350 for 15 minutes. Perfection! I also bumped up the seasoning; 1tsp. each rosemary, thyme and salt, 1/2 tsp. each black pepper and turmeric. I also added a huge clove of minced garlic. This is going into the rotation!

Awwww yeah, dude. For anyone who is looking for a relatively easy meal and wants to look like a boss, you can do this- here are some cheats (also, it looks like recipe amounts have been revised since some reviews. It's awesome with the listed amounts as of my review...not because of me, to be clear): I had most of this on-hand (miracle), but I didn't have fresh parsley. Use 1T dried. It's fine. I made my own biscuits. If you can find Fannie Farmer's Cookbook, get it. I'm sure there's a recipe on here, though. If you don't have buttermilk for biscuits, like me, it's okay- 1 Tb lemon juice per 1 c. milk (or ratio), mix, and let it set for 10 mins. It's really easier than it sounds- dry ingredients in a blender, add shortening, then add buttermilk in a bowl, flatten, cut circles, and you have biscuits. You'll look fancy, and you won't have to go to the store. The flour and butter thicken the sauce, but it's a light roux (basically), so make sure you use equal amounts. I had half-and-half, by some miracle, but if you don't, use milk for the creaminess, and reduce the broth in whatever amount you want as long as you have the same liquid amount. Just do 1 Tb cornstarch in 1/4 c. of cold water, and add it to your sauce mixture in the bubbling cook stage at the end before you add the chicken. That will thicken it. Don't get hung up on the amounts of veggies or chicken- use what looks good to you. It's your food. If you have frozen, and you are over your day, do it and don't give it a thought, except that there will be a little extra liquid, maybe, but not too terribly much. Thaw them first and drain the liquid. Please. If you screw it up now, don't blame me. You don't have to have everything for this. You can win this recipe. It's awesome. Rave reviews, straight-up, and I've never left a review here, not once.

That was really good. I haven't made chicken pot pie in years because my kids never liked it and I wasn't a fan of frozen vegetables. Using a fresh onion, carrots and celery made all the difference! Used a heaping TB of dried parsley and oat milk instead of half and half and it turned out awesome. Pre-cooked the biscuits for 8 minutes at 375 like someone else suggested and then turned them over when I put everything in the oven. Cooked everything in a cast iron skillet and put it right in the oven. Probably only cooked it for about 10 minutes, when the biscuits looked done. DH had 3 servings. Will make again for sure!

This recipe needs some work. If you're going to bake it, you need a 9x13 pan. It won't fit otherwise. ½ a cup of flour, not ¼ cup, or the roux will be too runny. As written, the bottom of the biscuits were completely raw and everything had to go back in the oven, prolonging an already long dinner.
I was short a cup of chicken so I added a potato that I baked in the microwave, I peeled and chopped the potato and added it to mixture before placing in the baking dish.

Like others, I found the filling to need more "thickening"... a rue, a touch of cornstarch, something. Also if you have big eaters or a big family, you'll want to double or triple the recipe. Instead of the flaky style biscuits, I went with the fluffy buttermilk style instead. And I broke them up into chunks, instead of laying them on whole. This solves the soggy bottom issue. Also, the recipe needs more "umph" .... the flavor is ok, but it's too heart-healthy. Add more salt, a bunch of garlic, and a touch of paprika. I also use a 5 pepper corn blend instead of just black pepper. I too cooked this all in one pan (cast iron Dutch oven, just left the lid off)... cooked the chicken first, removed from pan, then went as directed. Heavy cream instead of half and half adds some richness. Will definitely make again with these adjustments.

This is a favorite of ours on a cold night! I use a bag of frozen peas and carrots, about 2 tablespoons of dried parsley, and cooked the biscuits separately so they cook all the way through and aren’t soggy on the bottom. Definitely a keeper!
Filling is terrific but I’ve learned that you can’t cook the biscuits on top, if you do they are just soggy dough where it touches the filling. Bake them separately and serve on the side!

Soooo good! I used vegetable stock and omitted chicken to make it vegetarian. It was fantastic! I cooked the whole thing from start to finish in a Dutch oven, and I used only 4 biscuits that I cut into quarters. Baked for 25 mins and it was PERFECT!!!

We loved this recipe but I did make on change. I don't care for canned biscuits and after reading that so many had issues with them being raw on the bottom, I made drop biscuits and made them small but a lot. Still used the egg wash and it came out perfectly cooked!

I’ve made this countless times for my husband and I. We love it!! I just use a shallow Dutch oven to cook everything and just add the biscuits on top to bake in the oven. I also split the biscuits in half to cover more area. Thank you for this awesome recipe!!
I limited the mount of liquid, halved the biscuits and used a 9X13 casserole dish. Yummy

I loved this recipe, I added corn and went a little heavier on the veggies and it turned out really delicious! Also used Nicole’s tip of separating each biscuit in half so it covered my whole 9x13 baking dish which was a great move :)

The taste of this recipe is fantastic, however, we weren't able to fully enjoy it because the biscuits were undercooked on the bottom no matter how long it was left in the oven. It truly ruined the dish because it was not edible with the uncooked dough.
This was delicious. l cut the chicken broth + milk to 3 cups and the sauce was a perfect consistency. Even with less sauce, it needs to be cooked in a 9 x 13 pan, not 7 x 11.
So easy to put together. I cheated with frozen mixed veges and left over roast chicken, the sauce was delicious with the addition of cream. The family loved it!!

I doubled the recipe (for 5 people) and made some changes (use less flour). For seasoning next time I would use fresh thyme and rosemary. Also, I used frozen southern style biscuits (that I thawed). They hold up better and taste better than the canned biscuits. Thanks for the recipe!
Best Pot Pie ever and so easy! My family was more than pleased.
